notes.meaning: This is Benaiah son of Jehoiada, whose brave deeds are told just before. He was the most honored man among the Thirty, but he did not reach the level of the top three heroes. David made him head of his guard. This was the small band of soldiers who stayed close to the king to protect him.

Now the long list of David's brave fighters begins. They were the next rank of soldiers below the top heroes, and Asahel, Joab's brother, heads the list. The same list first appears in 2 Samuel 23, where Shammoth is called Shammah. Most of these men are not known from any other Bible story.

More names follow. Sibbecai is the same man called Mebunnai in 2 Samuel 23. These men were honored because of the good service they gave to their king and their country. As Matthew Henry puts it, the way to be great is to do good.

Maharai later led the group of soldiers who served the king during the tenth month of the year. Ithai came from Gibeah, in the land of the tribe of Benjamin. Many of the men in this first part of the list came from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.

The list goes on with more faithful fighters. These men did not win honor easily. They worked hard and risked their lives. In the same way, the honors of Christ's kingdom are for those who stay faithful and are willing to give everything for him.
More names are added. God was with David, and he often worked through people like these. He moved the hearts of able men to join David and help him become king.
The list continues. David had many strong men around him. Still, he did not give them the credit for his success. He gave the credit to the mighty God, whose presence is all in all.

Zelek was an Ammonite, a man from a people outside Israel. God's law said Ammonites should not enter the gathering of the Lord's people. Zelek must have proved so loyal to Israel that an exception was made. Matthew Henry sees this as a hint that Jesus, the Son of David, would have faithful followers among the nations too. Naharai carried Joab's armor. Joab himself is not on these lists, likely because as head of the whole army he ranked above them all.

Uriah the Hittite is named among David's brave men. Being on this list shows he was a fine and loyal officer. That makes David's later sin against him, taking his wife and arranging his death, even worse. Uriah's name is the last one on the list in 2 Samuel 23. From here on, Chronicles adds more names.

These added names are not in the list in 2 Samuel. They were still men of great courage and fame among David's leaders. Adina was a leader of the tribe of Reuben, with thirty captains serving under him. Many of these later names are linked to places east of the Jordan River.

Uzzia came from the town of Ashtaroth. It was in the land of the tribe of Manasseh, east of the Jordan. Shama and Jeiel came from Aroer, a town in the land of Reuben or Gad. So David's helpers came from many parts of the land.

Ithmah was a Moabite, another man from outside Israel who served David faithfully. Some of the place names here, like "Mahavite" and "Mezobaite," are hard to place today. The list ends here. Those who are faithful to Jesus, the Son of David, will have their names written down with far greater honor than these men.
